title: The AI Knows The Darkness of Our Hearts
subtitle: Maybe? Example of strange things happening using AI to try to make things simpler.
text:
So I'm using a program to take dictation and turn it into more well defined language and then a very strange thing happened here. And I wanted to share with you, because it's weird. I'm reading the introduction for a book thing may be where I take my podcasts and the ones that I did during the pandemic and I write some little introductions and suddenly have a book that's also an audiobook and that's kind of cool. But what happened when I try to record the introduction and let a I kind of rewrite it for me was unsettling. Without any further ado, this is what happened when I tried to explain the experience of recording an album and then running a psychiatric practice in the beginning of Covid in New York City, and you can see it goes pretty deep down a dark rabbit hole of some thing, but I'm not sure what:

What follows is a transcript created by an AI edit of my narration, and as you can see it was pretty strange pretty quickly:

Upon returning to New York City from recording a full-length album in San Francisco – my first real vacation in roughly a decade – the pandemic hit. This was at the start of 2020 and I’d celebrated New Year's Eve without my family, which felt strange. Shortly after this trip, news broke about global issues that were alarming and disconcerting. The album I'd recorded with John Vanderslice remained in existence but I did not do much with it as the world battle these unforeseen challenges.

Despite not being able to promote the album or perform any shows, I still had momentum from creating it. When COVID-19 struck, one way for me to navigate through was by producing narrative journalism podcasts. This book consists of those podcasts along with some accompanying commentary; edited so it’s more suitable as written content.

Our first broadcast aired on March 10th followed by quick successive ones on March 13th, 22nd and then others later that month. My colleagues helped create these stories as we switched our work practices to telehealth services except for interventional tasks.

During this time, Carlene, Michelle Bruenn (our admin) and myself migrated temporarily to Connecticut where we continued podcast production while experiencing an odd sense of exile. Meanwhile, my children stayed with their grandparents.

(It starts to get weirder and Weirder —OSM)

Additionally managing telehealth duties while running a practice proved challenging but necessary under circumstances which also saw the release of my new book on mentalization-based treatment even though I wasn't doing much with it nor with my recently recorded album.

This journey began because of my love for storytelling through recordings and given what unfolded during those times became about just that – life amidst a pandemic situation everyone eventually grew tired of both literally and metaphorically speaking
